subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which policy shape is approved for core?
rationale: The request changes browser egress controls and public config/UX semantics, and current code has no existing confirmation or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a staged core policy
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before considering interactive confirmation.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to an approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, audit, and redirect/rebinding semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation.

options.title: Reject core expansion
options.body: Keep strict default plus hostname exceptions and document broad private-network access as an explicit trusted-environment opt-in.

recommendation.title: Design a staged core policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking before considering interactive confirmation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the broadest current history across the browser SSRF resolver, shared SSRF guard, and security docs that define this boundary.
